"A 3D third-person shooter survival game. The player spawns in an island arena. There are 10 AI enemy bots roaming around. The player can walk, run, and shoot with auto-aim assist. Weapons and health packs are scattered on the ground for looting. A giant blue energy circle acts as the safe zone; it slowly shrinks towards the center of the map over time. If the player is outside the circle, they take continuous damage. The goal is to be the last one surviving. (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18:

20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

<!-- omgithub:readme:end -->

## Last Light — Island Survival

A complete, browser-playable 3D survival shooter. Drop into a low-poly island arena with ten AI rivals, loot weapons and medkits, and keep inside the shrinking blue safe zone. Be the last survivor.

### Play

Open `index.html` in a modern browser, or serve this folder over HTTP. Three.js is loaded from jsDelivr.

- **Desktop:** WASD or arrow keys to move, Shift to sprint, hold the mouse button to fire. Auto-aim assist tracks nearby rivals.
- **Phone/tablet:** use the left virtual stick to move and the on-screen Run and Fire buttons.
- Walk over glowing pickups to collect a weapon or restore health. Watch the tactical map and avoid the storm.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D third-person survival shooter for phones and tablets, based on the user’s island-arena, ten-enemy, loot, and shrinking safe-zone brief.

## Requirements
- Mobile/tablet support with usable touch controls.
- Ten AI bots, movement and sprinting, shooting with auto-aim assist, ground loot, shrinking blue safe zone with outside-zone damage, and last-survivor goal.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone browser game in `index.html`, using Three.js from jsDelivr.
- Designed a low-poly island and a responsive HUD; desktop uses WASD/arrows, Shift, and mouse fire, while touch devices use a virtual stick and Run/Fire buttons.
- Safe zone begins shrinking after 15 seconds and reaches its target radius at 120 seconds.

## Work State

### Completed
- Created a playable Three.js game with ten AI rivals, island terrain, loot, weapons, medkits, auto-aim, combat, a shrinking zone, damage, HUD, tactical map, and win/lose screens.
- Added responsive mobile controls and updated `README.md` with gameplay instructions.
- Validated JS syntax and ran the game in Playwright; latest console check reported zero errors and zero warnings.
- Captured and inspected gameplay screenshots at `screenshots/island.jpg`, `screenshots/gameplay.jpg`, and `screenshots/mobile.jpg`.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. If further work is requested, inspect `index.html` and test the requested change in-browser.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation and UI.
- `README.md`: Project and gameplay instructions.
- `screenshots/mobile.jpg`: Latest inspected mobile gameplay capture.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A local HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; browser testing used `playwright-cli`.
- The game requires network access to load Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.164.1/build/three.module.js`.

M README.md
?? .gitignore
?? Agents.md
?? capture.sh
?? index.html
?? start.sh
?? startup.sh

Sudah saya ubah agar game lebih cocok dimainkan dalam mode **landscape** di ponsel dan tablet:

- Saat perangkat dalam posisi portrait, muncul instruksi untuk memutarnya.
- Saat mulai bermain, game mencoba mengunci orientasi ke landscape jika browser mendukungnya.
- Tombol “COBA MODE LANDSCAPE” disediakan; jika penguncian tidak didukung, pemain tetap bisa memutar perangkat secara manual.
- Tata letak kontrol disesuaikan untuk layar landscape.

Pemeriksaan sintaks JavaScript berhasil. Catatan: penguncian orientasi bergantung pada dukungan browser dan biasanya hanya berfungsi setelah game dimulai.
